A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gradient-Guided Annealing for Domain Generalization and contain 23 readable pages, including the supplementary material. Text, equations, figures and tables support a reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v5 reports original synthetic classification experiments, GGA benchmark results, gradient-alignment and sensitivity analyses, and supplementary results including ColoredMNIST and RotatedMNIST.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experiments and analyses, including the authors' GGA results in the main text and supplementary tables.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 9 adds initialization of theta'_t to theta_(t-1), whereas v5 initializes only theta_t there. This provides a default candidate when the annealing search accepts no perturbation, a localized correction to the written procedure. The PDFs do not establish a change to the implementation used for the experiments.

E1.justification: Both retain the synthetic classification example, PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita and DomainNet, plus ColoredMNIST and RotatedMNIST in supplementary Table 9. No evaluated dataset, task or scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding main and supplementary tables, including ERM, IRM, Fish, SAM, GSAM and SAGM in their respective comparisons. The same combinations of GGA with baseline methods are reported.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 3 retain the same leave-one-domain-out evaluation, pretrained ResNet-50 backbone, Adam optimizer, training budgets and hyperparameters. Supplementary experimental procedures are also unchanged; no revised evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: The synthetic demonstration, VLCS gradient-alignment analysis and PACS sensitivity analysis are retained in Figures 1, 3 and 4. The questions tested and supporting evidence are unchanged, with no added or removed ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Run-count and seed statements and standard-error reporting are unchanged. Table 2 retains three-trial GGA combinations and five-trial standalone GGA reporting, while supplementary Section 8 retains five-run MNIST reporting.

E6.justification: Reported values, rankings and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains averages of 63.9 for ERM and 66.3 for GGA; supplementary Table 9 retains GGA averages of 51.9 on ColoredMNIST and 97.8 on RotatedMNIST.

T1.justification: Equation (5) replaces the minimum of a sum of pairwise cosine similarities with the minimum over distinct domain pairs. Algorithm 1 receives the same correction. This repairs the formal definition to match the existing minimum-pairwise description; the generative-model assumptions and derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about early gradient-guided annealing, competitive domain-generalization performance and benefits from combining GGA with existing methods.

C2.justification: The interpretations of gradient alignment, IRM's degradation and perturbation sensitivity remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning computational overhead, reliance on domain labels and batch-size dependence.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures in Section 4.1, Table 3 and supplementary Sections 7–8 retain the same hyperparameters, hardware, computational-cost description and integration instructions. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2 and supplementary Section 6 are unchanged. Reference differences concern page backreferences caused by text reflow, not added or removed research.

P1.justification: Section 3.3 changes 'highest gradient agreement' to 'highest minimum gradient agreement,' and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining prose and section ordering are retained, without substantial rewriting.

P2.justification: The corrected equation and pseudocode become more compact, reflowing surrounding material. Table 3 moves upward, the experimental section begins on page 5 instead of page 6, and references begin on page 8 instead of page 9. Figures and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 repairs the mismatch between the stated minimum-pairwise criterion and Equation (5)/Algorithm 1, and adds a default candidate initialization. These localized corrections improve the accuracy and usability of the method description. The empirical evidence and claims remain unchanged, so the overall quality gain is limited.
